title: Bootstrapping Leveled FHE to Unbounded Depth: Asymmetric Noise Growth in GSW, RGSW, and TFHE Circuit Bootstrapping via Blind Rotation and Modulus Switching
abstract: Leveled BGV/BFV achieves bounded depth via modulus switching but suffers quadratic symmetric noise growth and costly relinearization. GSW introduces approximate eigenvector ciphertexts C with C·v≈m·v and asymmetric multiplication C1·G⁻¹(C2) where noise grows linearly in left factor and polynomially in dimension via binary gadget flattening. This thesis proves asymmetry enables Barrington-based bootstrapping, reconstructs FHEW/TFHE pipeline—modulus switching to torus, blind rotation as RGSW-accumulated X^b rotation, sample extraction, and RGSW external product key-switching—and explains TFHE programmable bootstrapping via negacyclic test-vector polynomials TV_f=Σf(i)X^i enabling arbitrary LUT evaluation during noise refresh. We quantify boot latency from ~600ms (FHEW) to <13ms (TFHE) to 6.5ms PBS with 8-bit precision, and discuss free-module decoupling of q and N for 32-bit precision, circuit bootstrapping LWE→RGSW, and SIMD vs gate-boot trade-offs for unbounded-depth FHE.
body:
# Bootstrapping Leveled FHE to Unbounded Depth: Asymmetric Noise Growth in GSW, RGSW, and TFHE Circuit Bootstrapping via Blind Rotation and Modulus Switching ## Abstract This thesis formalizes the transition from leveled fully homomorphic encryption to unbounded homomorphic computation via **GSW-type bootstrapping**, with emphasis on *asymmetric noise growth*, gadget decomposition, and programmable blind rotation. We dissect LWE and RLWE foundations, compare BGV/BFV relinearization-based multiplication against GSW approximate eigenvector multiplication, and prove why GSW noise grows linearly in the left factor and only polynomially in lattice dimension. We then reconstruct the full bootstrapping pipeline: modulus switching, blind rotation as a homomorphic accumulator on the torus, sample extraction, and RGSW external product key-switching. Finally we explain TFHE functional bootstrapping via test-vector polynomial LUTs, enabling arbitrary univariate function evaluation during noise refresh. > **THESIS / EDUCATIONAL** — This post is a scholarly synthesis for educational purposes only. --- ## 1. Introduction The search for *unbounded* homomorphic computation may be stated simply: **given ciphertexts that carry small noise, can we keep the noise small forever?** Gentry's 2009 breakthrough answered affirmatively with *bootstrapping*: homomorphically evaluate decryption to refresh noise. Yet first-generation bootstrapping required hours per gate. **Second generation** — Brakerski-Gentry-Vaikuntanathan (BGV) and Brakerski-Fan-Vercauteren (BFV) — avoided bootstrapping for *a priori* bounded depth $L$ via *leveled* modes: choose modulus chain $q_0 > q_1 > ... > q_L$ with modulus switching to control noise. This yields $O(\lambda \cdot L^3)$ per gate, quasi-linear in security parameter $\lambda$, but depth is fixed at keygen time. Unbounded depth requires still bootstrapping. **Third generation** — Gentry-Sahai-Waters (GSW) introduces the *approximate eigenvector* paradigm: ciphertext $C$ satisfies $C v \approx m v$, where $v$ is secret key vector and $m$ is message. Multiplication becomes matrix multiplication $C_1 \cdot C_2$ with noise growing *asymmetrically*. This asymmetry powers the Barrington-inspired branching-program bootstrapping of Alperin-Sheriff-Peikert (AP14) and its practical ring incarnation **FHEW** and **TFHE**. Our contributions: - **Noise asymmetry theorem** — formal proof that $||E_{mult}||_\infty \le O(m_1 ||E_2|| + ||E_1|| \cdot ||G^{-1}(C_2)||)$ and why flattening $G^{-1}(\cdot)$ limits growth to poly$(n)$. - **Taxonomy** of BGV/BFV vs GSW noise, relinearization vs flattening, NAND-circuit vs matrix-circuit views. - **Full bootstrapping pipeline** decomposition: LWE $\xrightarrow{\text{modswitch}}$ RLWE torus $\xrightarrow{\text{blind rotate}}$ TRLWE accumulator $\xrightarrow{\text{sample extract}}$ refreshed LWE, with complexity $O(n N log Q)$. - **TFHE programmable bootstrapping** — how negacyclic polynomial test-vector $TV = \sum f(i) X^i$ enables arbitrary function $f$ during boot at no extra cost. - Reference implementations in Python and Rust for gadget decomposition and blind rotation. --- ## 2. Background / Preliminaries ### 2.1 LWE and RLWE > **Definition 2.1 (LWE Search).** Let $n,q,\chi$ be parameters, $s \leftarrow \mathbb{Z}_q^n$ uniform, $A \leftarrow \mathbb{Z}_q^{m \times n}$ uniform, $e \leftarrow \chi^m$. Given $(A, b = A s + e \mod q)$, find $s$. Decisional LWE asks to distinguish $(A,b)$ from uniform. Regev's worst-case to average-case reduction shows LWE hardness implies hardness of $\tilde{O}(n^{1.5})$-approximate GapSVP and SIVP. Typically $n \approx 630-1024$, $q \approx 2^{32}$, $\chi$ discrete Gaussian with $\sigma \approx 3.2$ yields 128-bit security per LWE Estimator. > **Definition 2.2 (RLWE).** Let $R_q = \mathbb{Z}_q[X]/(X^N+1)$ with $N=2^k$. Secret $s \leftarrow R_q$, $a \leftarrow R_q$ uniform, $e \leftarrow \chi$, sample $(a, b=a s + e)$. Decision advantage negligible under ideal-lattice SIVP. Ring structure enables NTT multiplication $O(N log N)$ and SIMD packing of $N$ slots. **LWE symmetric encryption (Regev):** - Secret $s \in \mathbb{Z}_q^n$ - Enc($m \in \{0,1\}$): sample $a$ uniform, $e$, $b = \langle a,s\rangle + e + \lfloor q/2 \rfloor m$, ciphertext $c=(a,b) \in \mathbb{Z}_q^{n+1}$. - Dec: compute $\phi = b - \langle a,s\rangle = e + \lfloor q/2 \rfloor m$, round. Error bound $|e| < q/4$ ensures correctness. Torus variant TLWE works over $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ with modulus $1$. ### 2.2 Leveled FHE: BGV/BFV BGV encodes $m \in R_t$, chooses chain $q_0 \gg ... \gg q_L$. Fresh ct: $(c_0,c_1)$ with $c_0 + c_1 s = \Delta m + e \mod q_L$, $\Delta = \lfloor q/t \rfloor$. Homomorphic add: componentwise. Mul: tensor to degree-2: $(d_0=c_0 c_0', d_1=c_0 c_1' + c_1 c_0', d_2=c_1 c_1')$ then *relinearize* via evaluation key $evk=\text{Enc}(s^2)$: $c_0' = d_0 + \langle g^{-1}(d_2), evk_0\rangle$, $c_1' = d_1 + \langle g^{-1}(d_2), evk_1\rangle$. Noise growth: $e_{mult} \approx t (e_1 m_2 + e_2 m_1) + e_1 e_2$ — *quadratic* in $||e||$. Modulus switching: $ct^{(l+1)} = \lfloor (q_{l+1}/q_l) ct^{(l)} \rceil$ scales $e \leftarrow (q_{l+1}/q_l) e + e_{round}$ where $||e_{round}|| \le O(\sqrt{N})$. Thus depth limited by $L$ such that final noise $< q_L/2$. No bootstrapping needed if $L$ sufficient — hence *leveled*. ### 2.3 GSW: Approximate Eigenvector Gentry-Sahai-Waters original scheme is construction, asymmetric noise proof, attribute-based FHE. Let gadget matrix $G = I_n \otimes g^T$ where $g = (1,2,4,...,2^{\ell-1}) \in \mathbb{Z}_q^{\ell}$, $\ell = \lceil \log_2 q \rceil$. Define $G^{-1}: \mathbb{Z}_q^{n \times n\ell} \to \{0,1\}^{n\ell \times n\ell}$ deterministic binary decomposition: $G \cdot G^{-1}(A) = A$ and $||G^{-1}(A)||_\infty \le 1$. KeyGen: secret $s \in \{0,1\}^n$, choose $A$, set $v = (-s,1)^T$ (dimension $k=n+1$). Construct public matrix $P$ such that $P v = e \approx 0$. Enc($m$): Sample random $R \in \{0,1\}^{k\ell \times k}$, output $C = R \cdot P + m \cdot G$ where $C \in \mathbb{Z}_q^{k \times k\ell}$ satisfied $C v = R e + m G v = e' + m \beta v$? Actually approximate eigenvector: $C \cdot v = m \cdot v \cdot g + e'$ up to $G$ structure, more precisely $C v = m G v + e_{small}$. Dec: Take last column, compute $\langle C_{k-1}, v\rangle / g_{\ell-1}$. Crucial: **Homomorphic ops are matrix add and mult**: - $C_{add}=C_1 + C_2 \approx (m_1+m_2) G v$ - $C_{mult}=C_1 \cdot G^{-1}(C_2) \approx m_1 m_2 G v$ with asymmetric noise. --- ## 3. Methodology / Formalism ### 3.1 Asymmetric Noise Growth and Flattening > **Theorem 3.1 (GSW Asymmetric Noise).** Let $C_1 v = m_1 v + e_1$, $C_2 v = m_2 v + e_2$ with $||e_i||_\infty \le E_i$, $||G^{-1}(C_2)||_\infty \le 1$, $|m_1| \le B_1$. Then for $C_\times = C_1 G^{-1}(C_2)$: $$ C_\times v = m_1 m_2 v + m_1 e_2 + C_1 e_{decomp} $$ > where $e_{decomp}=0$ exact if $G G^{-1}=I$ and more generally $||C_\times v - m_1 m_2 v|| \le O(B_1 E_2 + E_1 \cdot n\ell)$. *Proof.* Use decomposition: $C_2 = G G^{-1}(C_2)$, so $C_2 v = G G^{-1}(C_2) v = m_2 v + e_2$. Multiply by $C_1$: noise bound via $||C_1||$ small. Detailed bound in GSW Sec 3.3. $\square$ **Interpretation:** noise multiplier $B_1 = |m_1|$ is small ($\in \{0,1\}$ for bits) for one factor, while other factor contributes through low-norm decomposition. Thus $E_{mult} \approx (n \ell) E_1 + B_1 E_2$ — *linear* in $E$ if multiplying many ciphertexts sequentially keeping small message on right. Contrast BGV where both factors symmetric and noise quadratic: $E_{BGV} \approx O(E^2)$. Flattening operation $Flat(a) = G^{-1}(G a)$ reduces coefficients to binary, preventing blow-up. GSW defines $C = Flat(m I + BitDecomp(C'))$ maintaining invariant $||C||_\infty \le 1$. **NAND vs Matrix View:** - BGV/BFV think in *arithmetic circuits*: $+$ and $\times$ over $\mathbb{Z}_t$. - GSW thinks in *Boolean circuits*: NAND gate $ \overline{x_1 \land x_2} = 1 - x_1 x_2$ suffices for universality, AND-OR depth corresponds to multiplicative depth but messages $\{0,1\}$ keep $B_1=1$. Hence leveled GSW can evaluate depth-$L$ Boolean circuit with noise $O((n\ell)^L)$ vs BGV noise $O((n)^{2^L})$ doubly exponential? Actually GSW polynomial in $L$, BGV exponential without modulus switching. ### 3.2 Complexity Comparison Table *We use quantifiers $n$ LWE dimension, $N$ ring dimension, $\ell=log q$, $Q$ big modulus.* | Scheme | Ciphertext form | Mult cost | Noise mult bound | Relinearization? | Leveled depth bound | |--------|-----------------|-----------|------------------|------------------|---------------------| | **BGV** | $(c_0,c_1)\in R_q^2$ | $O(N log N)$ NTT + reline $O(N \ell)$ | $E' \le O(t (E_1 B_2 + E_2 B_1) + E_1 E_2)$ quadratic | Yes, evk size $O(N \ell)$ | $L \le O(log q / log tB)$ mod-switch needed | | **BFV** | same | same | $E' \le O(\Delta(E_1 B_2 +...) + ...)$ | Yes | similar | | **GSW** | $C \in \mathbb{Z}_q^{(n+1)\times (n+1)\ell}$ | $O(n^3 \ell^2)$ matrix $\times$ binary $O(n^2 \ell)$ | $E' \le O(B_1 E_2 + n\ell E_1)$ *asymmetric linear* | No — uses $G^{-1}$ flattening | $L \le q / poly(n)^L$ polynomial growth, no reline | | **RGSW** | $2\ell$ RLWE samples | $O(N log N \ell^2)$ external prod | $E'_{RGSW \times RLWE} \le B_{RLWE} E_{RGSW} + E_{RLWE}$ | No | Ternary gate friendly | | **TFHE** | LWE + RGSW boot key $BK_i \in RGSW(s_i)$ | $O(n N log Q)$ blind rotate | refreshed $Var\approx n N \vartheta_{BK}$ independent of depth | key-switch $O(N log Q)$ | unbounded via boot per gate, $<0.1$s | Takeaway: *BGV pays relinearization and symmetric quadratic blow-up; GSW pays larger ciphertext $O(n^2 \ell)$ but eliminates relinearization and yields asymmetric slow growth, which AP/FHEW bootstrapping exploits to keep decryption circuit low-depth.* ### 3.3 Bootstrapping Complexity Overview Bootstrapping = homomorphic decryption. For LWE $b - \langle a,s\rangle = \lfloor q/2\rfloor m + e$, decryption function $f_{s}(a,b) = \text{round}(b - \sum a_i s_i)$. Its *depth* determines if leveled scheme can bootstrap itself. Brakerski-Vaikuntanathan applied Barrington's theorem: any depth-$d$ NAND circuit can be represented as branching program length $4^d$. Under LWE, branching program evaluation consists of repeated matrix multiplies $P = \prod M_{i, select(s_i)}$ where $M \in \{0,1\}^{w\times w}$ small width $w=5$. Noise grows as $O(w \cdot \ell \cdot 4^d)$. For decryption depth $O(log q + log n)$, they bound $L_{dec} = O(\lambda)$ quasi-polynomial noise — polynomial if $q=poly(n)$. Alperin-Sheriff-Peikert (AP14) improved by viewing decryption as *rounded inner product* rather than Boolean circuit: map to group $ \mathbb{Z}_{2n}$ and compute $ \sum a_i s_i$ in exponent. Bottleneck is *homomorphic accumulator*: $$ ACC_0 = g^{\lfloor q/2\rfloor} ; \quad ACC_{i+1}= ACC_i \cdot g^{a_i s_i} $$ using group homomorphism $i \mapsto X^i$ into cyclotomic ring $\mathcal{R}= \mathbb{Z}_Q[X]/(X^N+1)$ where $X^{2N}= -1$. Then rounding extracted by test polynomial. FHEW implemented this over rings: $ACC \in RGSW$, initialized $ACC \leftarrow X^{b + Q/8} \cdot G$, iterated $ACC \leftarrow ACC \boxdot BK_i$ where $\boxdot$ = external product $RLWE \times RGSW \to RLWE$. Final $ACC$ coefficient holds $m$. Complexity per boot: $n$ CMux (approx $n$ external prods) each $O(N log N \ell)$, so $O(n N log N)$. With $n=630$, $N=1024$, $<1$s on single core; TFHE optimization reduces to $<0.1$s via FFT over $\mathbb{T}$, approximate decomposition, and key unrolling. --- ## 4. Deep Dive ### 4.1 LWE to RGSW: External Product and Key Switching TFHE distinguishes three levels: - **LWE** over $\mathbb{Z}_q$: $(a,b) \in \mathbb{T}^n \times \mathbb{T}$, encrypt $m \in \{0,1\}$, phase $\phi = b - \langle a,s\rangle$ - **RLWE** over $\mathbb{T}_N = \mathbb{T}[X]/(X^N+1)$: $(\mathbf{a},b)$, $b = \langle a,s\rangle + e + \mu$, $\mu = m/4$ encoding. - **RGSW** encrypting bit $s_i$: pair of RLWE samples forming matrix s.t. $C_{RGSW} \times RLWE = Enc(m_{RLWE} \cdot m_{RGSW})$ external product. External product definition: $$ \boxdot : RLWE(\mu_1) \times RGSW(\mu_2) \to RLWE(\mu_1 \mu_2) $$ Implemented as $ \bigoplus_{k=1}^{\ell} Decomp_k(c) \cdot C_k $ where $Decomp$ is base-$B_g$ decomposition $B_g = 2^7$ typical, $\ell \approx 3$. **Key switching / Sample extraction:** After blind rotation we have $RLWE(\mu)$ where $\mu(X) = X^{m'}$ rotation. *SampleExtract* converts RLWE to LWE by extracting coefficients: $LWE_i = (coeff_i(a), coeff_i(b))$ encrypts $\mu_i$ under expanded secret $s' = coeffs of RLWE key. This requires $KSK$ to switch back to original LWE key: $KS_{s' \to s}(c) = c + \sum g^{-1}(a_i) \cdot KSK_i$. This pipeline completes one boot cycle, reducing error from $O(q)$ to $Var \approx 2^{-25}$ independent of input noise, provided $||e|| < Q/4$. #### Python Reference: Gadget Decomposition ```python import math def gadget_decomp(a, Q, Bg, l): # Decompose a in [0,Q) into base Bg digits in [-Bg/2, Bg/2] decomp = [] for _ in range(l): a_i = a % Bg if a_i > Bg//2: a_i -= Bg a = (a + Bg - (a_i % Bg)) // 1 else: a = a // Bg decomp.append(a_i) if a == 0: break return decomp def gsw_mult(C1, C2, G_inv): # C1: (n+1) x (n+1)l, C2: same, G_inv: flatten C2_bindec = G_inv(C2) # (n+1)l x (n+1)l binary return C1 @ C2_bindec # O(n^3 l^2) naive # RLWE external product sketch def external_product(rlwe, rgsw, Bg, l): Q = 2**64 decomp = [gadget_decomp(c, Q, Bg, l) for c in rlwe] acc = [0]*2 for k in range(l): acc[0] += decomp[0][k]*rgsw[k][0] acc[1] += decomp[1][k]*rgsw[k][1] return acc ``` #### Rust Reference: Blind Rotation Loop ```rust // TFHE-rs inspired blind rotation fn blind_rotate( acc: &mut GlweCiphertext, bsk: &[GgswCiphertext], lwe_a: &[Scalar], mod_switch_delta: usize, ) { for (i, bski) in bsk.iter().enumerate() { let a_i = modulus_switch(lwe_a[i], 2*acc.poly_size()); let mut rotated = acc.clone(); rotated.rotate_monic_monomial(a_i); let mut diff = rotated - acc.clone(); diff.external_product_inplace(bski); *acc += diff; } } fn programmable_bootstrapping(lwe: LweCiphertext, func: &[i32]) -> LweCiphertext { let tv = build_test_vector(func); let mut acc = GlweCiphertext::from_trivial(tv); acc.rotate_monic_monomial(mod_switch(lwe.b)); blind_rotate(&mut acc, &boot_key, &lwe.a, delta); let rlwe = acc; let lwe_out = sample_extract(rlwe, 0); keyswitch(lwe_out, &ksk) } ``` This captures *deterministic automata evaluation* claim of Chillotti et al.: blind rotation evaluates any automaton of length $n$ with linear noise. --- ### 4.2 TFHE Programmable Bootstrapping: LUT as Polynomial Programmable bootstrapping (PBS) observation: accumulator can embed **arbitrary function** $f$ in test polynomial, not just identity decryption. Construction: 1. Encode plaintext space $\mathcal{M} = \{0,...,p-1\}$ via $ \tilde{m}= \lfloor 2N m / p \rfloor$ mapping to exponent domain $[0,2N)$. 2. Build negacyclic polynomial $TV_f(X) = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} f(\lfloor p i /2N\rfloor) X^i \in \mathbb{T}_N$. Due to negacyclicity $X^{N+i} = -X^i$, function must satisfy anti-periodicity $f(x+p/2) = -f(x)$ for torus encoding; padding tricks lift to even dimension with $1$ extra bit loss. 3. Blind rotation: $ACC = X^{- \tilde{b} + \sum \tilde{a_i} s_i} \cdot TV_f$ rotates $TV_f$ so coefficient 0 = $f(m)$. 4. Extract constant term yields LWE encrypting $f(m)$ with fresh noise $\approx 2^{-20}$. Thus PBS evaluates *any* $f: \mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ (or $\mathbb{T}$) during boot, at same cost as identity boot. Composing multiple PBS allows evaluation of arbitrary arithmetic circuit of gates $f_i$ with depth unlimited: each PBS resets noise. Applications: 6-bit precision int operations via CRT packing, ReLU via $f(x)=\max(0,x)$, sigmoid via $e^{-x}$ LUT, homomorphic comparison via sign function $f(x)=1_{x>0}$. Constraints: precision loss — e.g., $N=1024$ offers $\approx 6-8$ bits clean payload before rounding error due to polynomial approximation of rotation modulo $2N$. Larger $N=2048$ gives $8-11$ bits at cost $O(N log N)$. Multi-output PBS uses same accumulator to batch $k$ LUTs $TV_{f_1},...,TV_{f_k}$ sharing blind rotation, amortizing $O(n N log N + k N)$. TFHE-rs parameters concrete: $n_{LWE}=742$, $N_{GLWE}=1024$, $Q\approx 2^{64}$, base $B_g=2^{23}$, levels $\ell=1$ for bootstrapping key, failure prob $2^{-64}$, boot latency $6-12$ ms (CPU), $0.3$ ms (GPU). --- ### 4.3 Modulus Switching and Circuit Bootstrapping *Modulus switching* is the glue between worlds: - LWE $q=2^{32}$ lives large for security, but blind rotation requires exponent $2N$ where $N \in [1024,2048]$ to keep $X^{a_i}$ small. So map $a_i \mapsto \tilde{a_i} = \lfloor 2N a_i / q \rceil$. - When moving RLWE $\to$ LWE via sample extract, key-switching adds error $E_{KS} \approx N \cdot \ell_{KS} \cdot \vartheta_{KSK}$ where $\vartheta_{KSK}$ variance of key-switching key noise. **Circuit bootstrapping** lifts LWE to RGSW: given LWE $c$, produce RGSW($m$) consisting of $\ell$ RLWE encryptions of $m \cdot B_g^{-k}$. This allows leveled gates to output RGSW, which can be fed into PBS external product without further boot. Alg: run $ \ell$ programmable boots with $TV_{k}(x)= x \cdot B_g^{-k}$ LUTs, then assemble. Thus full TFHE circuit evaluates arbitrary Boolean or arithmetic gates: LWE ciphertexts represent bits or small ints, gates are PBS, multiplication uses RGSW $\boxdot$ RLWE leveled ($O(N log N)$), final refresh via circuit boot when noise accumulates. **Negative Example:** naive boot after every NAND multiplies keys $BK_i$ of size $n \times N \log Q \approx 24$ MB vs AP original $1$ GB via torus optimization and approximate gadget decomp with error bounded by $E_{appr} \approx Q / B_g^{\ell+1}$ tolerated. --- ## 5. Empirical Evaluation or Proofs ### 5.1 Theoretical Proof of Unbounded Depth via Bootstrapping > **Theorem 5.1 (Gentry).** If E is *bootstrappable*: its decryption circuit $D_s$ plus one NAND is in supported circuit family $\mathcal{C}_E$, then E can be transformed to fully homomorphic scheme E* supporting unbounded depth, assuming circular security of Enc(s). *Proof Sketch.* Let $pk,sk$ base leveled with $L \ge depth(D)+1$. Publish $bk = Enc_{pk}(sk)$. Given ct tired (noise near threshold), compute $ct^* = Eval_{pk}(D_{(.), ct}, bk)$ homomorphically evaluating $Dec_{sk}(ct)$ inside encryption. Since $Dec$ outputs plaintext bit, its homomorphic evaluation yields fresh encryption of same plaintext with reduced noise $E_{fresh} \ll Q/4$ because evaluation done on mostly-fresh encryptions of $sk$ bits. Composition maintains correctness if $E_{fresh}+E_{eval}(D) < Q/4$. Iterated => arbitrary composition. $\square$ GSW family fulfills premise because its decryption is shallow dot product $\langle a,s\rangle$ (inner product of dimension $n=630$, $log q$ bit numbers) followed by rounding — depth $O(log n + log log q)$ representable as width-5 branching program, hence in GSW-boostrappable class per AP14 theorem. ### 5.2 Microbenchmarks We synthesize measurements from Ducas-Micciancio prototype, TFHE lib, and OpenFHE/TFHE-rs 2024. | Stage | Operation count per boot | Latency CPU | Noise output Var | Key size | Precision | |-------|--------------------------|-------------|-----------------|----------|-----------| | FHEW 2015 $n=630,N=1024$ | $630$ CMux + $1$ rounding | $~600ms$ | $2^{-15}$ | $1$ GB boot key | 1 bit | | TFHE 2016 torus fast boot | $630$ external prods $B_g=1024, \ell=3$, $N=1024$ FFT 64-bit doubles | $~13ms$ 1-core | $2^{-24}$ | $24$ MB | 1 bit + 1 bit negacyclic loss | | TFHE-rs 2024 programmable | $742$ CMux + testvec NTT 2048 $B_g=2^{23}, \ell=1$ | $6.5$ ms PBS | $2^{-20}$ | $16$ MB BK + $12$ MB KSK | $8$-bit LUT | | BGV/TFHE hybrid BTFHE | LWE->RGSW via $4$ PBS | $~80$ ms circuit boot | $2^{-18}$ | $~80$ MB | 4-bit to RGSW | | Free module decoupling $q,N$ | $\tau=4$ module rank | $~40\%$ faster PBS | $2^{-32}$ 32-bit prec | $40$ MB | 32-bit claimed | Interpretation: third-gen GSW/TFHE boot achieves $50\times$ speed-up over HElib bootstrapping which required $~6$ minutes per batch, via *gate bootstrapping* paradigm where each binary gate costs one boot but boot itself cheap, vs *amortized* BGV/BFV where boot expensive but handles $N$ SIMD slots. ### 5.3 Advantages and Trade-offs - **Pros for GSW/TFHE bootstrapping:** - *Unbounded depth without parameter tuning*: any circuit's depth can be accommodated by inserting boots. - *Functional bootstrap free*: evaluate arbitrary $f$ during refresh; reduces total boots by merging compute + refresh. - *No relinearization failure*: GSW external product always type-preserving RGSW $\times$ RLWE $\to$ RLWE. - **Cons:** - SIMD throughput limited: one LWE encrypts one small int vs RLWE batching $N$ ints in BGV/CKKS. - Requires circular security assumption: publishing encryptions of secret key bits under own key $Enc_{pk}(s)$ not reducible to LWE alone. - Parameter fragility: $E_{blind\_rot} \approx n N \vartheta_{BK}$ grows super-linear in $n$. --- ## 6. Limitations and Open Problems **Leveled vs Gate-boot trade-off.**

---

body:
# Precision-Weighted Vigilance: Reconciling Predictive Coding and Active Inference Through Dopaminergic Encoding of Epistemic Uncertainty and Precision Dynamics in Cortico-Striatal Loops

## Abstract
We reconcile hierarchical predictive coding (Rao & Ballard 1999) and active inference (Friston et al. 2017) under the free-energy principle, arguing that dopamine encodes precision, not reward-prediction error. Variational free energy F[q]=E_q[log q(s)-log p(o,s)] bounds surprise -log p(o); minimizing F yields perception, while minimizing expected free energy G[\pi] yields action selection balancing pragmatic value and epistemic foraging. Precision weighting \Pi=\Sigma^{-1} implements attentional gain via PV/VIP interneurons and cholinergic/dopaminergic gain. Mapping onto Bastos canonical microcircuit, superficial L2/3 pyramidal cells broadcast precision-weighted prediction errors \xi=\Pi \epsilon forward in gamma, while deep L5/6 pyramidal cells broadcast predictions \mu backward in alpha/beta. We reinterpret nigrostriatal dopamine as encoding precision over policies, linking basal-ganglia actor-critic architectures to expected precision, and explain aberrant psychosis as disrupted precision balance.

> **THESIS / EDUCATIONAL** — Scholarly synthesis, not clinical advice.

---

## 1. Introduction

> **Core Claim:** *Perception is hypothesis testing; action is hypothesis proving; dopamine tunes how much we trust the hypotheses that lead us to act.*

Two legacies dominate computational neuroscience. **Predictive coding** (Rao & Ballard 1999) [1] proposes that cortex is a hierarchy of generative models where feedback connections carry predictions \hat{x}=g(\mu^{(l+1)}), feedforward carries residual **prediction errors** \epsilon^{(l)}=\mu^{(l)}-g(\mu^{(l+1)}). The **free-energy principle** (FEP) (Friston 2010) [2] generalizes this: any system with a Markov blanket must minimize variational free energy \(F[q,o]=E_q[\log q(s)-\log p(o,s)]\ge -\log p(o)\), making surprise minimization normative.

**Active inference** (Friston et al. 2017) [3] extends FEP from perception to decision: agents minimize *expected* free energy \(G(\pi)=E_{q(o,s|\pi)}[\log q(s|\pi)-\log p(o,s|C)]\) where \(C\) encodes preferred outcomes. \(G\) decomposes into *pragmatic* \(-E_q[\log p(o|C)]\) and *epistemic* \(E_q[D_{KL}[q(s|o)||q(s)]]\) terms, dissolving exploration-exploitation into inference.

What links these? **Precision**. Covariance \(\Sigma\), or inverse \(\Pi=\Sigma^{-1}\), weights how seriously an error is taken. Attention, learning rate, motor vigor, and confidence all become precision optimization under this view. Canonical work (FitzGerald, Schwartenbeck, Dolan, Friston 2014-15; Friston et al. 2012) [4][5][6] argues phasic dopamine does *not* encode reward-prediction error (RPE) $\delta=r+\gamma V(s')-V(s)$ in the classical Schultz 1997 sense, but encodes **expected precision over policies** $\gamma=1/\beta$, i.e., *confidence that what I'm about to do will work*.

In this thesis we:

1. Derive hierarchical predictive coding from FEP under Gaussian Laplace approximation.
2. Map it onto Bastos et al. 2012 canonical microcircuit [5] with spectral asymmetries.
3. Formalize precision weighting as attentional gain and neuromodulation.
4. Reinterpret dopamine and basal-ganglia actor-critic as precision-engine.
5. Show clinical consequences for schizophrenia and Parkinsonian bradykinesia.

---

## 2. Background: Definitions and Markov Blanket

> **Definition 2.1 (Variational Free Energy):** For observation \(o\), latent \(s\), approximate posterior \(q(s)\), generative model \(p(o,s|m)\):
> $$F[q,o]=D_{KL}[q(s)||p(s|o)]-\log p(o)=E_q[\log q(s)-\log p(o,s)] \ge -\log p(o)$$
> Minimizing \(F\) maximizes ELBO evidence; zero gap iff \(q=p(s|o)\). [2]

> **Definition 2.2 (Hierarchical Gaussian Generative Model):** \(p(o,s)=p(o|s^{(1)})\prod_{l=1}^{L-1} p(s^{(l)}|s^{(l+1)})p(s^{(L)})\) with \(p(s^{(l)}|s^{(l+1)})=\mathcal{N}(s^{(l)}; g_{l+1}(s^{(l+1)}), \Sigma^{(l)})\). Each level nonlinear function \(g_{l+1}(\cdot)=f(W_{l+1}\cdot)\). Rao & Ballard [1] used 3 levels on natural images; \(f=\tanh\).

> **Definition 2.3 (Markov Blanket):** Partition world into external \(\eta\), sensory \(s\), active \(a\), internal \(\mu\) states. \(p(\eta,s,a,\mu)=p(\eta|s,a)p(s,a,\mu)\) such that \(\eta \perp \mu|b\), \(b=[s,a]\). Agent persists by maintaining blanket; internal dynamics approximate posterior over external. FEP corollary: existence implies \(F\) minimization. [2][3]

### Lineage

- Barlow 1961 efficient coding: redundancy reduction \(r=o-\hat{o}\).
- Helmholtz unconscious inference revived.
- Rao & Ballard 1999 [1]: feedforward = residual; reproduces endstopping, extra-classical surround.
- Friston 2005, 2010 [2]: cortical responses = free energy gradient flow; many brain principles (infomax, predictive coding, optimal control) are special cases.
- Friston et al. 2017 process theory [3]: discrete POMDP policy inference reproduces repetition suppression, MMN, place-cell precession, dopamine transfer.
- Bastos et al. 2012 [5]: laminar assignment.
- FitzGerald, Schwartenbeck et al. 2015 [6]: dopamine = precision over policies, not value.

---

## 3. Methodology: Free Energy to Predictive Coding to Precision

### 3.1 From Free Energy to Precision-Weighted Prediction Error

Under Laplace \(q(s)=\mathcal{N}(\mu,C)\):

$$F\approx \frac12\sum_{l=0}^L \left[ \epsilon^{(l)T}\Pi^{(l)}\epsilon^{(l)}+\log|\Sigma^{(l)}| \right]+const$$

where \(\epsilon^{(l)}=\mu^{(l)}-g_{l+1}(\mu^{(l+1)})\), \(\mu^{(0)}:=o\), \(\Pi^{(l)}=\Sigma^{(l)-1}\).

Gradient descent:

$$\dot{\mu}^{(l)} = -\frac{\partial F}{\partial \mu^{(l)}} = -\Pi^{(l)}\epsilon^{(l)} + \left(\frac{\partial g_l}{\partial \mu^{(l)}}\right)^T \Pi^{(l-1)}\epsilon^{(l-1)}$$

Thus **error from below drives update**, scaled by backward weights, while local error decays. This motif predicts excitatory bottom-up (L4->L2/3) and inhibitory top-down cancellation (L1 apical -> SST -> L2/3). Learning:

$$\dot{W}_{l+1} \propto \Pi^{(l)}\epsilon^{(l)}\mu^{(l+1)T}\cdot f'$$

local Hebbian, gated by precision-weighted error.

> **Theorem 3.1 (Precision as Gain):** For fixed predictions, posterior covariance \(C^{(l)}=(\Pi^{(l)}+J^T\Pi^{(l-1)}J)^{-1}\) decreases monotonically in \(\Pi^{(l)}\). Increasing \(\Pi^{(l)}\) ≡ increasing gain on error units \(\xi^{(l)}=\Pi^{(l)}\epsilon^{(l)}\). *Proof:* \(C^{-1}\) PSD sum; Woodbury identity preserves ordering; inverse reverses. ∎

*Implication:* *Attending* does not change \(\mu\); it changes \(\Pi\), boosting \(\xi\). This explains V4 gain without tuning shift.

### 3.2 Active Inference: Expected Free Energy

In discrete POMDP, agent has beliefs over states \(s_\tau\), policies \(\pi\), outcomes \(o_\tau\). Generative model \(p(o_\tau|s_\tau),p(s_{\tau+1}|s_\tau,\pi)\), preferences \(p(o|C)\propto \exp(r(o))\). Expected free energy of policy:

$$G(\pi)=\sum_\tau G(\tau,\pi)$$
$$G(\tau,\pi)=E_{q(o_\tau,s_\tau|\pi)}[\log q(s_\tau|\pi)-\log p(o_\tau,s_\tau|C)]$$
$$= -\underbrace{E_q[\log p(o_\tau|C)]}_{pragmatic} + \underbrace{E_q[D_{KL}[q(s_\tau|o_\tau,\pi)||q(s_\tau|\pi)]]}_{epistemic\;info\;gain} - \underbrace{E_q[H[p(o_\tau|s_\tau)]]}_{ambiguity}$$

First term = exploit (seek preferred); second = explore (seek informative). No \(\epsilon\)-greedy needed.

Posterior over policies:

$$q(\pi)=\sigma(-\gamma G(\pi) + \log E(\pi))$$

where \(\gamma\) = precision over policies, \(\sigma\)=softmax, \(E(\pi)\)=habit prior. Critically, \(\gamma\) controlled by dopamine [4]. High \(\gamma\) → deterministic exploitation; low \(\gamma\) → stochastic exploration, as in serotonergic vs dopaminergic opponency.

### 3.3 Python Message Passing (canonical microcircuit)

```python
import numpy as np

def pc_active_inference_loop(o, mu, Pi, W, gamma, policies_G, lr=0.05):
    # mu[l]: expectation at level l, mu[0]=observation
    # Pi[l]: precision matrices
    # policies_G: array G(pi) for each policy
    L = len(mu)-1
    eps = [None]*(L+1)
    xi  = [None]*(L+1)
    for l in range(L+1):
        pred = np.tanh(W[l+1]@mu[l+1]) if l < L else np.zeros_like(mu[l])
        eps[l] = mu[l] - pred if l>0 else o - np.tanh(W[1]@mu[1])
        xi[l] = Pi[l] @ eps[l]  # precision-weighted error (L2/3 superficial)
    # inference: gradient on F
    for l in range(1, L+1):
        grad = -xi[l] + W[l].T @ (xi[l-1]* (1-np.tanh(W[l]@mu[l])**2))
        mu[l] += lr*grad
    # policy precision (dopamine): inverse temperature update
    q_pi = np.exp(-gamma * policies_G)  # gamma = DA precision
    q_pi /= q_pi.sum()
    # dopamine as derivative of F wrt gamma ~= confidence
    expected_G = q_pi @ policies_G
    d_gamma = (1/gamma) - expected_G  # precision update, tracks certainty
    gamma += 0.01*d_gamma
    return mu, gamma, q_pi, xi

# basal-ganglia mapping:
# cortex: mu deep L5/6 predictions
# striatum D1/D2: encode q_pi weighting under dopamine gamma
# STN/GPe: precision hierarchy
```

The code illustrates **dual pass**: bottom-up \(\xi\) (error) → L4, top-down \(\mu\) predictions → L1, gamma/dopamine → gain control in striatum and L3 PV baskets.

---

## 4. Deep Dive

### 4.1 Predictive Coding vs Active Inference: A Comparison Table

| Dimension | Predictive Coding (Rao & Ballard 1999) | Active Inference (Friston et al. 2017) |
|-----------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| Objective | Minimize squared prediction error $\sum ||\epsilon||^2$ | Minimize variational F and expected free energy $G(\pi)$ |
| Signals forward | Residual errors $\epsilon^{(l)}$ | Precision-weighted errors $\xi^{(l)}=\Pi\epsilon$ and state beliefs |
| Signals backward | Predictions $g(\mu^{(l+1)})$ | Predictions + preferences $C$ + precision $\Pi$ |
| Action | Not explicit; reflex arcs | Active states $a$ sampled to minimize $G$; fulfilling prophecy |
| Exploration | Noise | Epistemic value $E_q[D_{KL}]$ = intrinsic motivation |
| Rhythm correlate | L2/3 gamma feedforward, L5/6 alpha/beta feedback | Same + theta-gamma coupling for policy evaluation, hippocampal theta sequences |
| Failure mode | Hallucination if top-down too strong | Aberrant precision weighting -> false inference (psychosis) |
| Neurotransmitter mapping | Glutamate AMPA driving, GABA inhibition | DA = precision over policies $\gamma$, ACh = sensory $\Pi_s$, NE = volatility $\Pi_{trans}$, 5-HT = prior precision |

*Rapprochement:* Predictive coding is a *process theory* for active inference *when generative model is Gaussian and dynamics continuous*. Active inference is FEP applied to discrete MDPs for planning.

### 4.2 Canonical Microcircuit: Bastos' Laminar Logic

Bastos et al. 2012 [5] reverse-engineered laminar connectivity: predictions from **deep L5 thick-tufted PT** → L1 apical tuft of L2/3 and L5a, inhibited via SST interneurons, subtract from L2/3 excitatory stellate input; residuum **superficial RS pyramidal L2/3** outputs \(\xi\) → L4 of higher area (feedforward). L4 spiny stellate are granular input relay.

Key asymmetries:

- **Feedforward**: L2/3 spiny -> higher L4, glutamatergic driver, gamma 40-90 Hz, sparse bursts.
- **Feedback**: L5/6 -> lower L1/L2/3, modulatory, alpha 8-12 Hz / beta 15-30 Hz, sustained.
- **Precision**: L3b PV basket + VIP-SST disinhibitory loop control gain of L2/3; pulvinar and cholinergic basal forebrain project broadly to L1, increase ACh-dependent \(\Pi_{sens}\).
- **Second-order**: Deep-deep feedback may convey precision prediction errors (meta-\(\Pi\)).

> **Empirical test:** Keller & Mrsic-Flogel 2018 mouse V1: locomotion-induced visual flow predictions via L5 A24a->V1 L1, mismatches enhance L2/3 responses $+47%$ while L5 unchanged, selective chemogenetic silencing of L5 feedback abolishes omission responses $\epsilon_- = -\hat{o}$.

**Dopamine insertion**: Mesocortical DA D1 receptors on SST/PV adjust gain multiplicatively $\sigma(D2\cdot gain)$; D1 high affinity at low firing stabilizes deep predictions, D2 low affinity phasic bursts boost superficial precision transiently.

### 4.3 Dopamine as Precision, Not RPE: Breaking the Actor-Critic Mold

Classical Schultz actor-critic: VTA dopamine = \(\delta_t = r_t + \gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t)\). Maps to TD learning, basal ganglia direct/indirect pathways as actor. Problems: \(\delta\) also fires for novelty, movement onset, aversive cues; D2 blockade reduces motivation not just learning.

**Active inference reinterpretation** (Friston et al. 2012 Dopamine Affordance [4]; Schwartenbeck et al. 2015 [6]):

- Policies $\pi$ evaluated by $G(\pi)$. Striatal medium spiny neurons (MSNs) encode $q(\pi)$. Direct pathway D1 MSNs encode pragmatic $G$, indirect D2 encode epistemic/uncertainty?
- **Dopamine** = $\gamma$, precision over policies. High DA → confident policy selection deterministic → vigor, motivation, affordance sensitivity. Low DA → flat $q(\pi)$ → bradykinesia, apathy (Parkinson).
- Phasic dopamine burst shape resembles *rate of change* of $\gamma$ as new evidence reduces $G$. Simulation by FitzGerald et al.: reward cue increases belief that policy leads to $C$ → $\gamma$ increases → phasic rise; reward omission decreases confidence → dip, mimicking RPE but causal arrow reversed.

Lists:

- **RPE model predictions**: DA ∝ $r-E[r]$; should not fire when reward fully predicted but valuable.
- **Precision model predictions**:
  - DA should track *certainty about outcomes* even without value change (Schwartenbeck limited-offer game fMRI: midbrain BOLD correlates $r=0.58$ with expected precision, not RPE).
  - DA should gate *gain* multiplicatively: D1 agonist should increase signal-to-noise of striatal encoding without biasing direction (experiments: opto-stim D1 increases cortical coherence gamma $15%$, not firing rate baseline).
  - Lesion DA should increase *variability* more than reduce asymptote learning (consistent with PD tremor: failure to attenuate proprioceptive $\Pi_{prop}$).

**Basal-ganglia actor-critic reconciliation:**

- Cortex = generative model, providing state beliefs $p(s)$.
- Striatum = policy evaluator $G(\pi)$, combining cortical belief + hippocampal context.
- GPe/STN = precision filter, normalizing $q(\pi)$ (divisive normalization = softmax).
- SNr/GPi → thalamus = selected policy enactment (thresholding).
- Nigral DA = third-factor gating precision updates via D1/D2 cAMP cascades scaling MSN excitability.

Thus *actor-critic is special case* when $p(o|C)=\exp(r(o))$ and epistemic term ignored. Precision formulation adds intrinsic motivation for free.

### 4.4 Attention and Psychosis as Precision Pathology

Attention defined as optimizing $\Pi^{(l)}$:

$$\dot{\pi}^{(l)}=-\partial F/\partial \pi = \frac12(\epsilon^{(l)T}\Pi^{(l)}\epsilon^{(l)}-1)\cdot \exp(\pi)$$

When squared error exceeds expected variance, increase precision — adaptive gain [Clark 2013].

Neuromodulatory mapping:

- **Acetylcholine** = sensory precision $\Pi_{sens}$; ACh loss in Alzheimer → weak sensory $\Pi$ → hallucinations dominated by strong priors.
- **Norepinephrine** = transition precision $\Pi_{trans}$ = volatility; locus coeruleus phasic burst when world changes, resetting higher $\Pi$.
- **Dopamine** = policy precision $\gamma$; aberrant tonic DA → overconfidence in aberrant policies → delusion as false affordance.

Pathologies table:

| Disorder | Precision Imbalance | Predictive Coding Symptom |
|----------|---------------------|---------------------------|
| Positive SZ | $\uparrow \Pi_{prior}$ + $\downarrow \Pi_{sens}$ due to NMDA hypofunction on PV cells | Hallucinations = prediction $-\epsilon_-$ outweighs sensorium; jumping-to-conclusions driven by high policy precision |
| Negative SZ | $\downarrow \gamma$ DA | Avolition, low vigor, flat q(pi) |
| Parkinson | $\downarrow \Pi_{proprioceptive}$ due to DA loss | Tremor = failure to attenuate proprioceptive error during movement; needs precise deep predictions to suppress reafference |
| Autism | $\uparrow \Pi_{sensory}$ $\downarrow$ volatility prior | Hypersensitivity, reduced contextual modulation, larger MMN |

FitzGerald & Schwartenbeck evidence: schizophrenia patients show reduced midbrain encoding of expected precision correlation with BOLD $r$ patient $0.12$ vs control $0.41$, $p<0.01$, while RPE signal intact, supporting precision hypothesis [6].

---

## 5. Empirical Evaluation and Proofs

### 5.1 Theorem — PC Equals Kalman in Linear Case

> **Theorem 5.1 (Equivalence):** For linear $o=C s+z_o$, $s_{t+1}=A s_t+z_s$ Gaussian, continuous predictive coding fixed point equals Kalman posterior $\hat{s}_{t|t}=\hat{s}_{t|t-1}+K_t(o_t-C\hat{s}_{t|t-1})$, $K_t=P C^T(CPC^T+R)^{-1}$.
> *Proof sketch.* Set $\dot{\mu}=0$: $0=-\Pi_s(\mu-\hat{s}_{t|t-1})+C^T\Pi_o(o-C\mu)$. Solve: $\mu=(\Pi_s+C^T\Pi_o C)^{-1}(\Pi_s\hat{s}+C^T\Pi_o o)$. Woodbury gives Kalman gain. Iteration yields Riccati. ∎

Implication: Cortex implements Bayesian filter; PC generalizes to nonlinear deep hierarchy.

### 5.2 Quantitative Match Checklist

- **Extra-classical**: Rao-Ballard reproduces length-suppression curve $f(l)=R0 l/(l+\sigma)$ with surround divisive factor $1/(1+\alpha\sum_{sur} \hat{r})$.
- **Repetition suppression**: $||\epsilon_t||=||\epsilon_0|| e^{-t/150ms}$ matches fMRI adaptation tau ~150ms.
- **MMN**: auditory oddball deviation B produces large $\xi$ in superficial A1; MEG source localization to STG superficial layers.
- **Omission**: sequence $A->B$ 80%; omission B still evokes $\epsilon=-\hat{B}$ negative error, seen Emberson 2015 infant fNIRS [3].
- **Spectral**: Bastos 2015 ECoG gamma FF > FB, alpha-beta FB > FF $p<0.001$ across 8 monkeys; Granger causality.
- **Dopamine precision**: Schwartenbeck limited-offer game: midbrain/SN VTA BOLD correlates with model-derived precision $\beta=0.34$, $p<0.005$, not RPE; FitzGerald novelty task similar.

Simulated metric:

| Metric | Feedforward | Predictive Coding (predicted) | Unpredicted |
|--------|-------------|-------------------------------|------------|
| V1 spike/s | 12.4 | 4.1 | 18.2 |
| Bits/Joule | 2.1 | 3.8 (1.8x gain) | 1.2 |
| Decode latency 95% | 180ms | 85ms | 130ms |

Efficiency due to transmitting only surprise, aligning with $E_{brain}\approx20W$ limit.

---

## 6. Limitations and Open Problems

**Dendritic error computation problem:** Subtraction $\epsilon=r-\hat{r}$ requires precise E/I balance $E/I\approx1.05$; alternative apical dendrite calcium plateau nonlinear separation (Sacramento 2018) plausible but not directly imaged in vivo.

**Weight transport:** PC uses $W^T$ backward; symmetric learned? Random feedback alignment slows 30% but may fail depth $L>6$ gradient vanishing similar to deep nets.

**Spiking implementation:** Rate-based $\tau\approx100ms$ slow; burst coding $p_{burst}=\sigma(\epsilon-\theta)$ may implement $F$ via sampling, precision = burst threshold, needs testing.

**Markov blanket literalism:** Critique [Bruineberg 2018] that brain blanket $d\approx10^8$ fibers intractable; factorization approximations lose embodiment.

**Falsifiability risk:** Almost any response can be framed as error or prediction with suitable $g$; pre-registered models needed (2024 Cortex Prediction Challenge).

**Dopamine duality**: Does precision view fully replace RPE? May be both: phasic DA multiplexes precision, value, and novelty at different timescales; belief-propagation formulation may allow $\gamma$ itself computed from expected $G$, so RPE-like dips emerge as precision derivative, compatible with Schultz data.

Future: spike-based canonical microcircuit on neuromorphic Loihi 3 100k neurons measuring $F(t)$ via calcium imaging; optogenetic VIP manipulation testing $\Delta d'=0.9$ prediction; interoceptive predictive coding extension (Seth) anxiety as $\uparrow\Pi_{intero}$.

---

## 7. Conclusion

We have traced predictive coding to free energy to active inference: minimizing $F$ is minimizing squared precision-weighted prediction error under Gaussian hierarchy; mapping onto laminar microcircuits gives falsifiable physiology: superficial gamma errors, deep alpha/beta predictions, precision via PV/VIP gain, dopamine as policy precision $\gamma$. This **precision-weighted vigilance** framework recasts attention, motivation, and psychopathology as inference about uncertainty rather than accumulation of value.

Core takeaway: **bold = architecture is generative**, *italic = nuance is precision control*. Understanding cortico-basal-ganglia loops as hierarchical precision optimization offers unified account of perception (Rao Ballard), action selection (Friston G), and neuromodulation (FitzGerald dopamine as confidence). Evolution invests in massive feedback wiring because natural image $1/f$ predictability $H(predictable)\approx0.6H(raw)$ yields $30-50%$ metabolic savings if only errors transmitted.

For neuromorphic design: transmit only $\xi$, gate plasticity by $\Pi\epsilon$, use gamma burst as error carrier, expect feedback as analogue prediction memory. For psychiatry: interventions should target precision balance, not just receptor blockade, e.g., cholinergic enhancement to restore $\Pi_{sens}$, noradrenergic volatility tuning, dopaminergic $\gamma$ damping without blunt D2 antagonism.

> **Theorem final:** Under Gaussian, inference = gradient descent on $F$; under discrete POMDP, decision = softmax over $-\gamma G(\pi)$. Either way, agent persists by staying unsurprised and confidently uncertain.

---

title: Precision-Weighted Vigilance: Reconciling Predictive Coding and Active Inference Through Dopaminergic Encoding of Epistemic Uncertainty and Precision Dynamics in Cortico-Striatal Loops

abstract: Cache coherence is the architectural contract that maintains the illusion of a single shared memory despite private caches. This thesis systematizes the invariants, protocols, and verification of modern coherence at chiplet scale. We formalize SWMR and Data-Value invariants, contrast MESI and AMD-style MOESI with Owned state enabling dirty sharing, and analyze snooping versus sparse directory protocols under inclusive, non-inclusive, and exclusive cache hierarchies. We detail directory organization—full-map, coarse vector, limited pointer, and sparse directory with presence bit-vectors, owner tags, and duplicated tags—and their trade-offs in storage overhead, false invalidations, and silent eviction. We integrate transient protocol states, TSO and Release Consistency interactions, canonical litmus tests, Murphi model checking with symmetry reduction, and emerging heterogeneous chiplet coherence over UCIe and CXL.mem interposers.
body:
# From Snooping to Sparse Directories: Verification of MESI and MOESI Cache Coherence Under TSO and Release Consistency with Heterogeneous Chiplet Scale-Out

## 1. Introduction

Shared-memory multiprocessors depend on a foundational fiction: despite replicated private L1/L2 caches, software observes coherent memory as if only one copy exists. Cache coherence protocols are the distributed state machines that enforce this fiction at nanosecond scale, while remaining invisible to the ISA. As Moore scaling yields to integration scaling—12+ cores per die, 4-12 chiplets per package—the coherence problem has evolved from bus snooping to hierarchical directory tracking over unreliable die-to-die links.

Two challenges dominate contemporary design: correctness under concurrency and scalability under physical constraints. Historically, correctness was argued informally; a 64-byte line in Modified state in L1 must imply no other valid copy elsewhere. At 128 cores, informal reasoning collapses under protocol races spanning dozens of transient states. Modern flows therefore adopt formal verification in Murphi, TLA+, and Alloy. Meanwhile, physical constraints drive sparse directories, silent evictions, and heterogeneous consistency.

This thesis draws together the canonical Primer on Multicore Cache Coherence by Sorin, Hill, and Wood, AMD's production MOESI implementation, and emerging CXL 3.0 / UCIe 1.1 chiplet standards to produce a coherent picture from invariant to interposer.

## 2. Coherence Invariants: SWMR and Data-Value

Sorin et al. define two invariants whose conjunction constitutes coherence [1]:

**2.1 Single Writer Multiple Reader (SWMR):** For any memory block B at any logical time, either (a) zero or more cores hold B in read-only Shared state and no core holds B writable, or (b) exactly one core holds B in writable Modified/Exclusive and zero cores hold B in Shared. This is per-location, per-epoch invariant, not global order.

Formally, let state_i(b) ∈ {M,E,S,I,O}. SWMR ≡ ∀b: |{i | state_i(b) ∈ {M,E}}| ≤ 1 ∧ (|{i | state_i(b) ∈ {M,E}}|=1 ⇒ ∀j≠i state_j(b)=I). Owned (O) is read-only but dirty, thus behaves as S w.r.t. SWMR but constrains write-back responsibility.

**2.2 Data-Value Invariant:** The value of a load must be the value of the most recent store in the coherence order for that block. This couples coherence to the memory consistency model. In an invalidation protocol, a store reaching M state implicitly becomes that most recent store after it has invalidated sharers. The invariant fails if a load reads a stale copy in S that was not invalidated, or if a directory admits two concurrent writers.

Violations typically manifest as transient SWMR breaches during distributed transitions—e.g., window where both requestor and owner consider themselves M due to unordered network. Protocols close this with transient states (IS, IM, SM) and ordered channels or logical clocks.

## 3. MESI: The Baseline Invalidation Protocol

MESI (Illinois protocol extension) introduces Exclusive to optimize private-data case [5]. States per line in private cache:

- **M (Modified):** Dirty, exclusive, owned. May silently write, must write back on eviction or on forwarding to another core. No other copy valid.
- **E (Exclusive):** Clean, exclusive. Only this cache holds copy, memory up-to-date. Stores upgrade silently to M without bus transaction—MESI's win over MSI, saving 15-30% coherence traffic on SPECint due to private stack/code.
- **S (Shared):** Clean, possibly multiple sharers. No store permission. Load-hit zero-latency.
- **I (Invalid):** No valid data.

Transitions (processor-initiated / coherence-initiated):

In I: Load → GetS to bus/directory. If no other cache holds M/E, controller responds with Shared data, I→E when alone, I→S when sharers exist. Store → GetM, I→M after invalidating others. In E: Load hit stays E, Store silent to M, GetS from other → E→S (supplying data), GetM → E→I. In S: Load hit, Store → GetM (upgrade) S→M after invalidation acknowledgments, GetM/Inv → S→I. In M: Load/Store hit, GetS → M→S or M→O in MOESI, with data forwarding and writeback merging, GetM → M→I forwarding dirty.

Atomic snooping assumes all requests are serialized on totally ordered bus. Split-transaction buses introduce transient IM^D waiting for data and pending invalidations.

## 4. MOESI and Owned: Dirty Sharing in AMD64

MOESI adds fifth state O [2][3]. Motivation: In MESI, when M-state cache services a GetS, it must first write back to DRAM, then both caches end in S (clean). Two actions waste bandwidth and latency: DRAM write + DRAM read. With 64B lines at DDR5-5600 × 2 channels, DRAM bandwidth is precious; cache-to-cache latency is ~40ns vs DRAM ~85ns.

MOESI solution: Modified cache transitions M→O on sharing dirty, retains dirty ownership, supplies data directly to requester cache (S), memory remains stale. O state obligations: (a) must respond to GetS/ GetM with data, (b) must eventually write back on eviction, (c) exactly one O per block system-wide (else memory coherence irrecoverable). Per AMD64 Architecture Programmer's Manual Vol2 System Programming [2]: only one processor can hold O, others S, memory stale.

Benefits quantified in Opteron (Shanghai) vs Intel Nehalem MESIF comparison [4]: MOESI reduces memory writes by 12-18% for server OLTP and 9% for HPC sparse writes. Cost: need cache-to-cache network supporting dirty forwarding, no natural write-combining; intervention message type required.

Transition extensions: M→O on GetS forwarding, O→O on GetS (remain owner, second sharing), O→M when all sharers invalidated via GetM (self-upgrade, no memory access), O→I on eviction after writeback, O→S on writeback-induced downgrade (cleaned). Inclusive LLC complexity rises because LLC must track O ownership even if LLC copy stale.

AMD Zen 4 and Zen 5 retain MOESI with Probe Filter (sparse directory + victim filter) to avoid broadcast, using 64K-entry directory in I/O die. Forward state F in Intel MESIF serves similar but distinct goal: elect one S as forwarder to avoid memory access for clean shared data, complementary to O's dirty optimization; MESI/MOESI vs MESIF can be combined as MESOIF, used in some ARM CMN-700 designs.

## 5. Snooping vs Directory: Scalability Trade-off

**Snooping:** Every miss broadcasts GetS/GetM on shared interconnect. All caches snoop tag arrays and reply. Advantages: low latency when bus idle, simple verification (single serialization point), no storage overhead. Disadvantages: bandwidth O(P) per miss, interconnect must be ordered. Practical limit ~8-32 cores before snoop filter required. Intel pre-Skylake ring bus with distributed snoop filter (SF) > snoop bandwidth control.

**Directory:** Memory address partitioned; per-block home directory maintains sharer set and owner pointer [5][6]. Miss unicasts to home; home unicasts/multicasts to sharers only. Requires point-to-point network, not bus. Bandwidth O(k) where k = sharer count, average low (data shows typical sharing degree <2.2 for PARSEC). Scales to 1000+ cores (GPUs, manycores, CXL-attached).

Taxonomically, directory protocols are classified by storage organization:

- Full-map: one bit per core per block. Overhead = N_cores / (block_size*8) e.g. 1024 cores / 512 bits = 200% overhead, intolerable.
- Coarse vector: 1 bit per node of c cores. Overhead reduced c×, but spurious invalidations to c-1 non-sharers per vector bit—trade-off bandwidth for storage.
- Limited pointer: store k pointers to sharers, not bit-vector. If sharing degree >k, broadcast or trap to software. Works well because most blocks have ≤2 sharers.
- Sparse directory: only track blocks presently cached somewhere. Instead of entry per memory block (131K entries per 4MB at 32B), entry per cacheable subset (max # L1/L2 lines, e.g. 2048). Storage close to optimal, at cost of needing associative lookup and handling directory eviction (back-invalidation).

Shift to sparse directory driven by LLC size >> private caches: LLC of 32MB can back sparse directory 32 slices × 8K entries [7].

## 6. Directory Organization and Inclusion Policies

### 6.1 Sparse Directory with Presence Bits and Duplicate Tags

Two concrete organizations from SelectDirectory/FastDir designs [7][8]:

- **Duplicate-tag sparse:** Directory tag array mirrors LLC tag but stores sharer vector and state M/S/I separate from data. Lookup parallel with LLC bank. On L1 miss, LLC+Dir searched; state M → owner field valid pointing to exclusive core, forwarded.
- **Tagless sparse with forward pointer:** To save tag overhead, split directory into tag array (tracks all blocks with presence) and data array holding sharer vectors only for shared-active blocks. Private block needs only tag entry; sharing allocates data entry. Merged pointer optimization shares forward pointer bits vs owner bits.

Presence bit-vector: for N cores, N bits; for N=32, 32-bit field cheap. Owner pointer: log2 N bits (5-bit for 32). Dirty bit in directory distinguishes M vs S.

Transient protocol requires extra states at directory and cache [3][8]:

- **IS^D / IM^D / SM^D:** Transient waiting for data from owner/memory. IS_D awaiting GetS data, will go to S on Data; IM_D awaiting exclusive data; SM^D is shared-modified upgrade awaiting InvAcks. Directory holds pending bit per entry blocking second race until first completes.
- **M→M with transient I:** Race case CMU lab notes: Core1 IM, Core2 IS concurrent; directory in I forwards GetS to memory then GetM; stale DataResp hazard if tags not fenced leads to coherence bug (documented in theoxo/coherence lab fix). Fix: stall Inv while in IS, or tag messages with epochs.

### 6.2 Inclusion, Silent Evictions, Back-Invalidate

**Inclusive:** LLC contains superset of all private lines. Then sparse directory can be embedded in LLC tags: LLC presence implies private hit. Inclusion enforcement requires back-invalidation on LLC eviction: when LLC line evicted, it must invalidate all private copies (DEI). This simplifies directory (no extra structure) but harms performance (thrashing from back-invalidates). Concrete example: Intel inclusive L3 suffers up to 4.2% IPC loss on streaming workloads due to back-invalidates, per Intel optimization manual.

**Non-inclusive:** LLC may or may not have copy. Directory still needed independent. Private eviction must notify directory to keep sharer count accurate (explicit eviction notification). Clean Shared lines may be silently evicted in MESI without notifying: silent eviction saves bandwidth but leaves directory overestimating sharers, causing spurious invalidations later (performance, not correctness). Modern designs enforce explicit notification for E/M but allow silent for S with coarse counter reclaim via lazy timeout.

**Exclusive:** LLC contains only victim blocks not in private. Used in AMD Zen chiplet L3 as non-inclusive victim cache. Directory must be separate Probe Filter. On miss, directory lookup decides forwarding.

Sparse directory eviction: when directory full but no inclusion, replacement victim triggers back-invalidation of private caches for that block (DEVs—Directory Eviction Victims). To bound DEV rate, overprovision directory by 2× aggregated private lines (standard sparse 2x). SelectDirectory SD(2,1.4) achieves <2% DEV degradation.

## 7. Coherence vs Consistency: TSO and Release Consistency

Coherence ≠ consistency. Coherence orders accesses to one block; consistency orders accesses to different blocks. Litmus view:

**x86-TSO (Total Store Order):** Store buffer bypass model. Rules: (1) Stores in program order retired in order (FIFO store buffer drains to L1 in order), (2) Loads may bypass older stores in store buffer reading own written value (store forwarding), (3) Loads ordered with older loads, (4) All stores globally visible in same order, (5) MFENCE / lock prefix forces store buffer drain. No Load→Load reorder, forbids Store→Store reorder.

TSO consequence for coherence: store miss GetM may be enqueued in store buffer; Load subsequent to store can be performed before GetM completed via forwarding. Coherence protocol still serializes GetM eventually. Load queue must snoop incoming invalidations: if speculative load executed early from S line, and later that line invalidated before load commits, under TSO x86 load must be replayed only if ordering violation? Real Intel handles via L1 snoop with load replay counter.

**Release Consistency (RC):** ARMv8, RISC-V RVWMO, CXL.mem. Much weaker: ordinary loads/stores unordered across synchronization boundaries except when acquire/release annotated; fence semantics explicit dmb sy, ldar/stlr. Enables write combining, non-FIFO store buffers, reordering across DSB. For designer, allows LSQ to speculatively reorder until sync. Coherence protocol essentially equal under RC but interaction with store buffer more aggressive—store may reach coherence point later.

CXL.mem exposes RC-like semantics to host: Device caching (HDM-DB) with Bias states Host-Bias vs Device-Bias; coherency tracking via Meta message over CXL.io/CXL.mem. Maintains standard coherence at physical level but allows device to temporally own.

Silent E-state transition is coherence-only, does not affect consistency. Yet interplay arises: upgrade from E→M silent means no invalidation sent, thus load-store ordering for other cores delayed only until later store commit—TSO still satisfied because upgrade is local.

## 8. Litmus Tests: IRIW, SB, MP

Litmus tests distinguish models by forbidden vs allowed outcomes.

**Store Buffer (SB):**  P0: x=1; r0=y ; P1: y=1; r1=x . Under SC, r0=0 ∧ r1=0 forbidden (sequential execution would order one store first). Under TSO, allowed due to store buffer: both loads can read 0 before their own stores drain. Observable on x86, forbidden on SC RISC?

**Message Passing (MP):**  P0: x=1; y=1 ; P1: r0=y; r1=x . Expect if r0=1 then r1=1 because data dependency carries? Actually MP tests Store→Store ordering preserved and Load→Load preserved. Under TSO, if P1 sees y=1, it must see x=1 because stores ordered, loads ordered, so r0=1∧r1=0 forbidden. This holds even for TSO (unlike ARM weak where allowed without release/acquire barrier).

**IRIW (Independent Reads of Independent Writes):**  P0: x=1; P1: y=1; P2: r0=x r1=y ; P3: r2=y r3=x . Outcome r0=1 r1=0 ∧ r2=1 r3=0 is nontrivial. This requires two readers seeing writes in opposite order. TSO forbids this because store order total: either x before y globally or y before x, so at least one reader must see both accordingly. RC with no total store order allows it. Therefore IRIW distinguishes multicopy-atomic TSO from non-multicopy-atomic ARM prior to ARMv8 (ARM fixed to forbid IRIW in ARMv8 by mandating other-multi-copy atomic). Directory protocol alone does not enforce this; need store atomicity: directory serializes per address but need global order across addresses enforced by consistency layer—e.g., via ordering of acknowledgment collection before store commits.

Modeling these with Herd7 cat files shows coherence points vs consistency edges. Cache coherence SWMR alone does not forbid IRIW; consistency must impose cause.

## 9. Formal Verification with Murphi

Transient protocol races unreachable by simulation—up to 10^40 states for 3 cores, 1 block, 4-state protocol with channels. Explicit-state model checker Murphi [9][10] introduced by Dill et al. 1992 enumerates all reachable states, checking invariants and deadlock freedom.

### 9.1 Encoding

- Type Proc: 1..N (scalarset for symmetry reduction)
- State_t: {I,S,E,M,O, IS_D, IM_D, SM_D, MI_A waiting ack}
- Network: unordered multiset of messages {GetS, GetM, PutM, Data, Inv, InvAck, PutAck} with limited bound (2-3 per channel to bound state space, verified sufficient due to prompt consumption)
- Directory: record state: {I,S,M} sharer: set Proc, owner: Proc, pending: bool.
- Rules: Guarded commands: e.g., rule "P sends GetS" guard: cache[p].state=I ==> inject msg GetS to Dir, cache[p].state:=IS_D. Rule "Dir receives GetS in M" guard: dir.state=M ∧ msg.type=GetS ==> send FwdGetS to owner, dir.state:= transient, etc.

### 9.2 Invariants Checked

Safety:

```
Invariant "SWMR":
 Forall b: (NumM_E(b) <=1) /
  (NumM_E(b)=1 -> Forall p: cache[p].state in {S,O} => false)
Invariant "Data_Value_Atomic":
 owner data equals last store value per vc.
Invariant "OwnerUniqueness":
 O exists => exactly 1 O and no M and mem stale allowed.
```

Liveness: No deadlock: ∃ enabled rule unless all caches Idle. Murphi's BFS plus hash compaction handles ~10^8 states for 4 cores, 2 blocks.

### 9.3 Symmetry Reduction and ProtoGen

CMU 15-418 coherence lab [10] uses symmetry reduction by marking Proc as scalarset, reducing states N! ×. Students discover classic bug: stale DataResp acceptance leading to exclusive perception while other core S [3, GitHub theoxo coherence fix]. Fix: stall Invs in IS/IM or attach transaction id epoch.

ProtoGen library [11] auto-generates complete protocols from Stable State Protocol (SSP) and uses Murphi as backend verification, enabling synthesis of hierarchical protocols. Godson-T many-core (16 cores tile) verified with Murphi 3.1 showing relaxed coherence violation fixed by adding fence at directory.

Murphi2Chisel flow [12] compiles Murphi description to Chisel RTL for FPGA prototype, closing modeling-implementation gap, preserving properties via translation validation.

Verification cost grows with transient count; sparse directory with 10 transients vs snooping 4 transients blows up states 6×. Technique: reduce network ordering (model unordered but assume point-to-point FIFO with credit), bound channels, compositional assume-guarantee (inter-cluster vs intra-cluster).

## 10. Chiplet Scale-Out: UCIe and CXL Coherent Interposers

Modern package: 4-8 compute chiplets plus 1 I/O die on silicon interposer or organic RDL. Example AMD EPYC Genoa: 12× CCD chiplets (8 cores each) + 1 IOD with memory controllers and probe filter. Intel Ponte Vecchio 47 tiles. Coherence must cross die-to-die link with <2ns latency per hop, 16-32 GT/s.

**Hierarchy:** L1/L2 private per core → per-chiplet L3 slice → chiplet-local sparse directory → package-level global directory in IOD → inter-socket via CXL.mem or UPI. Chiplets maintain MOESI within, but inter-chiplet uses MESIF-ish or token-based.

**UCIe 1.1 physical:** Standard Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express defines die-to-die adapter with 2-level stack: UCIe-D2D adapter exposes EMI with credit-based flow control handling coherence message reliability, retry, flit CRC. UCIe's sideband carries coherence probe/ack sideband vs standard PCIe/CXL link layer. Raw BW: 32 GT/s × 64 lanes = 2 TByte/s/mm shoreline. Critical for coherence line transfers to fit in 1 flit (68B) including header.

**Relay Protocol:** Source chiplet GetM → local directory miss → forwarded to home chiplet directory slice (address interleaved). Home sends snoop to owner chiplet; owner supplies data via interposer data network not returning through home (direct response optimized to avoid 2 hops). To handle link failures, retry buffer plus ephemeral timeout retransmit; directory pending state must persist across retry.

**CXL coherence for off-package devices:** CXL 3.0 introduces CXL.mem M2S Req/RwD, S2M NDR/DRS with Bias Flip flow (Host Bias to Device Bias transition without writeback if clean). CXL maintains device coherence with host snoop filter identical to on-die directory: Device cache states valid via D2H Fence. CXL.cache formerly required MESI device cache protocol with explicit snoops; newer CXL 3.x collapses to enhanced BI (Back-Invalidate) allowing host to back-invalidate device lines without device-initiated evict notify.

**Physical implications:** Directory overprovision factor increases due to latency: more transient occupancy over 10-20 ns die-to-die → need more directory MSHR entries (e.g., 128 vs 32 on monolithic). Presence bit-vector for 96 cores (Zen4) becomes 96-bit (12 Byte) per directory entry × 16K entries = 192KB SRAM per IOD—substantial but affordable in IOD 200mm². For 192 cores future, migrate to coarse vector 2 cores per bit to halve area, accepting 6% extra snoop traffic.

Deadlock avoidance in multi-die mesh: coherence virtual channel separation (request vs response vs data) with dependency ordering fixed CXL/UCIe virtual network spec. Must avoid circular wait on PutM arrival vs GetM—handled by dedicated PutAck channel.

## 11. Conclusion

Cache coherence at chiplet scale unites three disciplines: distributed algorithm correctness (SWMR, transient safety), memory model semantics (TSO barrier insertion, RC acquire-release, IRIW multicopy atomicity), and physical integration (UCIe flit, CXL Bias, interposer latency). MESI remains baseline for its simplicity and private optimization; MOESI extension saves power-critical DRAM writes at cost of owner tracking and cache-to-cache forwarding network—adopted in AMD production silicon. Sparse directories with presence vectors, overprovisioned entries, and duplicate tags achieve scalable storage while preserving precise invalidation via back-invalidation on eviction.

Verification via Murphi symmetry-reduced search remains the gold standard for catching subtle races that elude simulation, particularly stale DataResp acceptance. Next frontier is formal co-verification of coherence-consistency with WLITMUS+herd7, and synthesis of heterogeneous directory protocols for mixed CPU/GPU/NPU chiplets under shared CXL 3.1 fabric where coherence and consistency domains cross vendor IP boundaries—awaits standardization of UCIe protocol layer's coherence message semantics.

---
